statement: The callback returned by Allow retains the pointer to the specific TwoStepCircuitBreaker receiver, so rebinding the caller's local pointer to a different wrapper cannot retarget it.
A shallow value copy of a TwoStepCircuitBreaker initially aliases the same inner CircuitBreaker pointer without aliasing the original wrapper's pointer field.
If the original breaker's OnStateChange hook overwrites the outer wrapper during beforeRequest, that in-progress beforeRequest still records the admission on the original breaker.
A replacement half-open breaker with matching generation and MaxRequests=1 can close on a redirected success even if it has admitted zero requests.
Restoring the saved wrapper value can make a previously redirected completion report to the original inner breaker if the original generation still matches.
A redirected callback can resolve the replacement's open timeout and deliver its half-open notification before discarding the outcome on a generation mismatch.
When the request rebinds the caller's local CircuitBreaker pointer, ordinary Execute completion calls the original receiver's classifier and accounts on that receiver.
When an admitted request rebinds the caller's local CircuitBreaker pointer and panics, Execute's deferred failure report still targets the original receiver.
Replacing the caller's Settings.IsSuccessful field after construction does not replace the function stored in the existing breaker.
A stored IsSuccessful closure can observe a change to a variable it captures by reference after breaker construction.
Invoking a retained Allow callback after overwriting its receiver with a zero-valued TwoStepCircuitBreaker panics when afterRequest attempts to lock the nil inner receiver's mutex.
A late matching half-open success after a caller stopped waiting closes the breaker only if it brings consecutive successes to at least MaxRequests.
For a ReadyToTrip invocation, lock identity follows the inner CircuitBreaker, so a shallow TwoStep wrapper copy that still points to that inner breaker re-enters the same mutex through Counts.
A manual retry of an Allow completion after a hook panic can resolve a different inner breaker if the captured wrapper is overwritten between invocations.
